title: Deep M5.5+ pairs showed no clear 7-30-day excess under regional time shuffles in ComCat, 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether a known excess of nearby deep earthquake pairs extends beyond seven days. We used 785 ComCat events deeper than 300 km with preferred magnitude at least 5.5 in 2000-2025. Pairs were within 200 km Earth chord distance and in the same year. We shuffled fixed times among locations within each year and 20-degree cell in 19,999 draws. In the separate 7-30-day window, 147 observed pairs compared with a null mean of 142.30 and a central 95% null range of 123-161. The upper-tail p-value was 0.3412. The first day had 110 pairs versus a null mean of 71.06, with p=0.00005. A ten-degree grid and a shifted grid also gave no clear 7-30-day excess. Removing the cell with most events left no clear late excess. This narrows the time interpretation of prior cumulative counts. It does not prove that delayed triggering is absent. Small samples, geographic grid choice, mixed magnitude scales and the time-exchange assumption limit the result. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, an independent arithmetic audit and a static figure support reproduction. External event records are not bundled.

display.caption: Observed pair counts and shuffle means with central 95% null ranges in separate time windows. These ranges are not confidence intervals for an effect. All panels use the same 785 deep events.

citations.reason: The prior cumulative pair-count result sets this follow-up question. We use the same fixed public source. Data overlap; this is not independent replication. No code copied.
Luo and Wiens (2020) report deep dynamic triggering within days. Our pair test does not identify triggered events or test their physical model.
Wimpenny and colleagues (2023) show limits of inference from sparse global aftershock samples; their main scope is intermediate depth.
